newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian sugar drops as trucks restart deliveries.
newsitem.headline: Indian sugar drops as trucks restart deliveries.

text.p: Sugar prices fell sharply on the local Indian market, as trucks began deliveries to markets again after a 10-day strike, traders said.

"The end of the truckers's strike has restarted deliveries of sugar from mills to the market, while local buying remained slow at the higher level," said Shantilal Dedhiya, secretary of Bombay Sugar Merchant's Association.
"Bombay market has witnessed arrivals of about 90 to 100 truck loads of sugar today," he said.Each truck load contains about nine to 10 tonnes of sugar.
Ready delivery sugar S-30 dropped 35 rupees to 1,315/1,365 rupees per quintal while M-30 moved down by 25 to 50 rupees to 1,375/1,425 rupees per quintal.
"Looking at the increased arrivals I am expecting a further drop in prices as buyers are keeping to sidelines expecting further declines," Dedhiya said.
Meanwhile sugar for mill delivery rose five rupees to 1,215/1,230 rupees per quintal on resumption of lifting at the mill level by traders following conclusion of truckers strike.
Overall market sentiment remained subdued at the close of the session.
